subject: note: I saw my father’s corpse about twenty minutes after he died almost exactly twenty years ago. His life was gone and finally his useless, meaningless suffering was over. He looked oddly beautiful. Small and shrunken, his skin brown and wrinkled, like some ancient wooden statue dug up from the earth.
note: As paradoxical as it might sound, the decision to end one’s life is a requirement of life in order to escape a life of indignity and incarceration, the life of the concentration camp.
note: As Freud writes elsewhere, hate is older…
